title: High-Energy Neutrinos from Black Hole Evaporation in Neutron Stars
hook: A new theory chains four wild ideas together: dark matter piling up in a neutron star, collapsing into a microscopic black hole, evaporating away — and leaving behind detectable neutrinos.
key_points: Dark matter can accumulate inside a neutron star and, if dense enough, collapse into a tiny black hole.
If that black hole evaporates (Hawking radiation) faster than it swallows matter, it releases exotic particles.
Those particles escape the star and decay into high-energy neutrinos.
The capture-collapse-evaporation cycle can repeat, falling into two distinct physical regimes.
The predicted neutrino spectrum peaks above roughly 10 TeV, concentrated toward the galactic center.
Predicted rates are small but could add up to a percent of the observed galactic neutrino flux.
content_html: A new arXiv preprint by Ioannis Dalianis traces a speculative but concrete chain connecting some of physics' strangest ideas. If dark matter particles pile up inside a neutron star and are dense enough, they could gravitationally collapse into a microscopic black hole. Should that black hole's Hawking evaporation win out over it swallowing more matter, the evaporation releases long-lived, exotic particles that escape the neutron star and decay into high-energy neutrinos.
extra_html: Dalianis models this cycle of dark-matter capture, black-hole formation, and evaporation repeating over and over, finding two distinct regimes set by how fast the trapped dark matter heats up versus how fast the collapse cycle repeats — including one regime where the dark-matter cloud reaches a temperature far exceeding the neutron star's own core. The resulting neutrino spectrum is predicted to be broad, peaking above roughly 10 TeV, with a galactic component concentrated toward the Galactic Center. The predicted event rates are small, but under favorable conditions could contribute at the percent level to the high-energy neutrino flux astronomers already observe from the galaxy — a new theoretical thread linking dark matter, neutron stars, and neutrino astronomy.

related.title: The First Exact Picture of a Black Hole Evaporating in Our Universe
related.hook: Physicists have finally worked out, in exact mathematical form, how a real 3D black hole's geometry evolves as it evaporates — previously solved only in toy 2D universes.

related.title: Catching the Ghost Particle
related.hook: Trillions of neutrinos stream through your body every second, yet they almost never touch anything. To catch even a few, physicists build some of the most audacious detectors ever conceived.

flashcards.prompt: What chain of events could turn a neutron star into a neutrino source, per this theory?
flashcards.back_html: Dark matter piles up inside the star, collapses into a microscopic black hole, which evaporates via Hawking radiation and releases particles that decay into high-energy neutrinos.

flashcards.prompt: What determines whether the tiny black hole evaporates instead of just growing?

choices.text: Whether Hawking evaporation dominates over the black hole swallowing more matter
How many neutrinos have already been detected from it

flashcards.explanation_html: When evaporation wins out over accretion, the black hole releases long-lived particles that escape the star and decay into high-energy neutrinos.

flashcards.prompt: Where does the predicted neutrino spectrum peak, and where is the galactic signal concentrated?

choices.text: Above roughly 10 TeV, concentrated toward the Galactic Center
Below 1 GeV, spread evenly across the whole sky
Only at the galaxy's north and south poles

flashcards.explanation_html: The model predicts a broad neutrino spectrum peaking above about 10 TeV, with the Galactic component strongly concentrated toward the Galactic Center.
